Compare the two vector extents of The source region of the Yellow River and the Jiuzhaigou earthquake zone, and calculate the percentage of their overlapping area relative to their respective total areas.
tasks.reference_solution_description: Load the Yellow River source-region polygon and the Jiuzhaigou earthquake zone boundary, intersect them, measure areas for each dataset plus the overlap, and compute the percentage of overlap relative to both inputs.

arguments.geodataset: The source region of the Yellow River

steps.comment: Load the Yellow River source polygon (data/Data/GeoData/YellowRiver_SourceRegion.shp).
Load the Jiuzhaigou earthquake polygon (data/Data/GeoData/Jiuzhai.shp).
Use the lightweight overlap tool to intersect the two regions and store the shared footprint for downstream area calculations.
Measure the total area of the Yellow River source region.
Measure the total area of the Jiuzhaigou earthquake zone.
Calculate the absolute size of the overlapping footprint.
Divide overlap area by the Yellow River source total to get the fractional coverage.
Convert the ratio into a percentage for easier reporting.
Repeat the ratio calculation using the Jiuzhaigou earthquake zone total area.
Convert the Jiuzhaigou ratio into a percentage.

arguments.title: Overlap between Yellow River Source Region and Jiuzhaigou Earthquake Zone

steps.comment: Map both regions and the overlap to visually confirm the percentages reported in the calculator outputs.

tasks.task_text: Identify all areas within the Weihe River Basin where the slope is greater than icon 5 and the distance to the nearest traditional village exceeds 20 kilometers. (You can first load the Wei River Basin Topographic Slope Classification Dataset and extract the boundary of the Wei River Basin Topographic Slope Classification Dataset as a vector polygon, then use select_features_by_spatial_relationship​ to extract all scattered points within the region, and create a 20,000‑meter dissolved buffer only for these points. Next, reload the Wei River Basin Topographic Slope Classification Dataset raster data and reclassify it to filter out values greater than 5. Then, use the rasterize_vector_tool​ to convert the resulting buffer into raster data with the same specifications. Finally, perform an overlay operation on these two raster datasets—using the reclassified Weihe raster data to subtract the rasterized buffer data—to obtain the final result.)
tasks.reference_solution_description: Load the Weihe slope raster and traditional village points, convert the raster footprint into a lightweight polygon to select overlapping villages, build a unified 20 km exclusion buffer, reclassify the raster to isolate slope classes >5, and subtract the buffered overlap from the steep-area totals.

steps.comment: Load the nationwide traditional village points (data/Data/GeoData/VillagesChina.shp) so we can check which ones fall on the Weihe slope dataset.

arguments.rasterdataset: Wei River Basin Topographic Slope Classification Dataset

steps.comment: Resolve the absolute path to data/Data/GeoData/WeiheBasin.tif so the downstream raster tools reference the correct slope grid.
Convert the Weihe slope raster footprint into a compact polygon boundary that can be used for vector selections.
Keep only the villages that fall inside the Weihe Basin boundary.
Build a fused 20 km exclusion buffer around the overlapping villages so the final mask removes every buffered area as a single geometry.
Create a binary raster where class value 1 marks every Weihe pixel whose slope class exceeds 5, and store the summary (including pixel area for later area calculations).
Mask the high-slope raster by the fused buffer to quantify how many steep pixels are disqualified because they fall inside the buffered exclusion zone.
Derive the square-kilometer size of a single classified pixel by dividing the high-slope area by its pixel count.
Convert the number of overlapping pixels into square kilometers using the per-pixel area derived above.
Subtract the buffered-overlap area from the total square kilometers of slope>5 pixels to report the eligible steep region that still satisfies the 20 km separation constraint.

tasks.task_text: Based on the Guangming District DEM (Shenzhen), identify all areas with a slope less than 5 degrees, and calculate the total area of these flat regions.
tasks.reference_solution_description: Resolve the Guangming DEM path, convert it to a slope raster, reclassify it so slopes below 5 degrees become a binary mask, then feed that mask into the raster-area tool to measure the flat terrain.

steps.comment: Resolve the catalog path to data/Data/GeoData/guangming.tif so downstream tools read the correct DEM.
Convert the Guangming DEM into a slope raster so slope thresholds can be evaluated in degrees.
Reclassify the slope raster so cells below 5 degrees become value 1 and all other slopes become 0.
Measure the cumulative area of all pixels coded as 1 (slope < 5 degrees), reporting the flat terrain in square kilometers.
